phenotypes.label: Cardiometabolic comorbidity with chronic pain
phenotypes.description: Common cardiometabolic multimorbidity—hypertension, hyperlipidemia, type 2 diabetes, coronary atherosclerosis, and stage 3 chronic kidney disease—co-occurs with chronic pain, fatigue, and low back pain. This reflects a general chronic disease burden; sexual activity–related findings may appear but are incidental to the core pattern.

phenotypes.label: Mixed clinical themes
phenotypes.description: This cluster blends unrelated conditions without a single clinical theme. It mixes dental/oral disease, candidiasis and other genitourinary infections, respiratory infections/bronchitis, metabolic comorbidities, and scattered outliers, so it does not represent a cohesive condition pattern.

phenotypes.label: Age-related ocular degeneration
phenotypes.description: Age-related ocular disease with prominent macular degeneration (exudative and nonexudative), cataract, vitreous degeneration/floaters, retinal drusen, and hypertensive retinopathy. Impacted cerumen and bilateral hearing loss often co-occur, consistent with sensory decline in older adults.

phenotypes.label: Anxiety, depression, and insomnia
phenotypes.description: Patients with mood and anxiety disorders with prominent insomnia, including generalized anxiety disorder, recurrent major depressive disorder (including remission), adjustment and acute stress reactions, and panic symptoms. ADHD and menopausal symptoms appear in some patients. This pattern is more common in females and skews slightly younger.

phenotypes.label: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and diabetes
phenotypes.description: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease with prominent metabolic risk: coronary atherosclerosis, chronic ischemic heart disease, and acute myocardial infarction co-occur with hyperlipidemia and abnormal glucose/diabetes. Diabetes-related complications such as retinopathy, mononeuritis, and adhesive capsulitis are represented, reinforcing a cardiometabolic cluster. This pattern is more common in males and skews older within the cohort.

phenotypes.label: Inflammatory bowel disease with malabsorption
phenotypes.description: Cluster centered on inflammatory bowel disease, especially Crohn’s, with intestinal complications such as obstruction, fistulas, perianal abscess, and postoperative states. Prominent malabsorption and nutritional deficits (vitamin B12, zinc), with related immune‑mediated gastrointestinal conditions (celiac disease, eosinophilic esophagitis) and extraintestinal features like erythema nodosum and enteropathic arthritis.

phenotypes.label: Cerebrovascular disease with cardiometabolic risk
phenotypes.description: Cluster of ischemic cerebrovascular disease (stroke/TIA) and carotid atherosclerosis occurring with hypertension, mixed hyperlipidemia, diabetes, and hypertriglyceridemia. Gout is a frequent comorbidity in this cardiometabolic risk profile. More common in older men.

phenotypes.label: ADHD, mood disorders, and injuries
phenotypes.description: Top conditions mix inattention/ADHD, anxiety–depression, and cognitive or emotional findings with numerous musculoskeletal injuries (wrist pain, mallet finger, ankle sprain) and assorted medical issues (chronic cough/diarrhea, endocrine abnormalities). These span unrelated body systems without a unifying clinical syndrome, so this cluster reflects multiple themes rather than a single phenotype.

phenotypes.label: Multiple sclerosis with neurogenic bladder
phenotypes.description: Pattern centered on demyelinating central nervous system disease, particularly multiple sclerosis, with sensory disturbances (paresthesia, anesthesia), weakness, ataxia, and gait instability. Neurogenic bladder features are common, including urge incontinence and overactive bladder; optic neuritis and neuromyelitis optica appear in some patients. This reflects MS-spectrum disease with functional mobility limitations.

phenotypes.label: Rheumatoid and osteoarthritis with osteoporosis
phenotypes.description: Inflammatory and degenerative arthritis centered on rheumatoid arthritis (often hand involvement) alongside hip osteoarthritis and peri‑trochanteric pain. Coexisting osteoporosis with fragility fractures (vertebral, femur) and upper‑limb tendon/nerve disorders are frequent, with an older age skew. Sicca features (xerostomia) and dental erosion suggest autoimmune overlap.

phenotypes.label: Epilepsy and intracranial injury
phenotypes.description: Seizure and epilepsy diagnoses co-occur with cognitive and language disturbances such as amnesia, aphasia, and altered mental status. The pattern centers on epilepsy and status epilepticus with etiologies and sequelae of intracranial injury and infection, including traumatic brain injury, subdural/subarachnoid hemorrhage, encephalitis, and postictal complications like aspiration pneumonitis and delirium. It is somewhat more common in males.

phenotypes.label: HIV/AIDS with STIs and opportunistic infections
phenotypes.description: HIV infection with frequent co-occurring sexually transmitted infections such as gonorrhea, syphilis, genital herpes, and HPV-related disease (anogenital warts). Opportunistic and infectious complications include oral candidiasis, herpes zoster, and tuberculosis, with associated peripheral neuropathy, renal dysfunction, and oral/dental disease.

phenotypes.label: Cervical radiculopathy and shoulder disorders
phenotypes.description: Cervical spine degenerative disease and radiculopathy cluster with shoulder pathology, presenting as neck and shoulder pain with radiating arm symptoms. The pattern includes cervical spondylosis/stenosis and disc degeneration alongside rotator cuff disease, impingement, adhesive capsulitis, and upper-limb neuropathic features. Patients often have muscle spasm and chronic pain manifestations.

phenotypes.label: Anxiety and depressive disorders
phenotypes.description: Anxiety and depressive disorders dominate, often co-occurring with fatigue, insomnia, and functional gastrointestinal complaints such as GERD and constipation‑predominant IBS. Chronic pain and asthma appear as additional comorbidities, with incidental minor injuries and localized infections in the background.

phenotypes.label: Thyroid and parathyroid disorders
phenotypes.description: Cluster of thyroid and parathyroid disease: nodular goiter, papillary thyroid carcinoma, and postoperative hypothyroidism. Accompanied by parathyroid disorders with calcium disturbances (hyper- or hypocalcemia) and primary hyperparathyroidism, plus neck mass and laryngeal or swallowing symptoms (dysphonia, vocal cord paralysis, dysphagia).

phenotypes.label: Psoriatic arthritis and enthesitis
phenotypes.description: Psoriasis with psoriatic arthritis is central, with prominent enthesitis and dactylitis. Patients have musculoskeletal pain and degeneration (shoulder and hip arthritis, spondylosis), elevated inflammatory markers, and frequent tendon/ligament injuries and distal radius/ulna fractures. Common comorbidities such as osteoarthritis, hypertension, and GERD also appear.

phenotypes.label: Acute musculoskeletal pain and injury
phenotypes.description: Acute, symptom-driven encounters centered on pain and musculoskeletal injury: generalized and regional pain (shoulder, wrist, ankle, back), radiculopathy/nerve root syndromes, soft-tissue swelling, fractures, and ligament or tendon lesions. It also includes concurrent infectious/respiratory complaints (fever, sore throat, COVID-19, wheeze) and generic chief-complaint coding, consistent with urgent or emergency presentations rather than chronic disease management.

phenotypes.label: Graves hyperthyroidism with ophthalmopathy
phenotypes.description: Endocrine phenotype centered on hyperthyroidism/thyrotoxicosis with Graves ophthalmopathy (orbit/eyelid involvement, exophthalmos) and toxic diffuse goiter, with abnormal thyroid function documented. Patients frequently have palpitations, supraventricular arrhythmias, syncope, and nonspecific symptoms; GERD, asthma, and musculoskeletal pain appear as accompanying comorbidities. This pattern is more common in females.

phenotypes.label: Breast cancer and menopausal breast disorders
phenotypes.description: Breast malignancy and benign breast disease with abnormal mammography, palpable breast lumps, and lymphedema. Patients are largely postmenopausal women and often exhibit menopausal symptoms (atrophic vaginitis, flushing) alongside bone health issues such as osteoporosis and fractures.

phenotypes.label: Urogynecologic and ear disorders
phenotypes.description: The leading conditions combine lower urinary tract symptoms and female pelvic organ prolapse (cystocele, rectocele) with unrelated ear complaints (impacted cerumen, hearing changes) and assorted minor issues. There is no single clinical theme across these conditions.

phenotypes.label: Atopic asthma and allergic rhinitis
phenotypes.description: Atopic airway disease with allergic rhinitis (pollen and animal dander), asthma across severities including cough-variant forms, and allergic conjunctivitis. Nasal symptoms (posterior rhinorrhea), cough, and occasional allergic reactions (e.g., insect stings) and ABPA appear within the same allergic spectrum. This pattern is more common in females.

phenotypes.label: Ocular surface and corneal disorders
phenotypes.description: Dry eye/tear film insufficiency with blepharitis and meibomian gland dysfunction, including keratoconjunctivitis sicca in Sjogren’s and in graft-versus-host disease. Corneal involvement is prominent (dystrophies, keratoconus, ulcers, HSV keratitis, scarring) with symptoms such as eye pain and epiphora. Eyelid disorders (hordeolum, ptosis, dermatochalasis) and cataract frequently co-occur.

phenotypes.label: Hand and foot arthritis and tendinopathy
phenotypes.description: Degenerative and inflammatory arthritis centered on the hands and feet, with foot/hand pain, osteoarthritis of the ankle/foot, and synovitis/tenosynovitis. Includes tendon and forefoot disorders such as trigger finger, Achilles tendinitis, and hallux valgus/rigidus, alongside seronegative rheumatoid arthritis and inflammatory polyarthropathy.

phenotypes.label: Lymphoid leukemia plus metabolic baseline
phenotypes.description: Leading conditions split between a lymphoid malignancy and hematologic autoimmune cluster (chronic lymphocytic leukemia, lymphocytosis, immune thrombocytopenia, autoimmune hemolytic anemia, lymphadenopathy, splenic lesions) and a common cardiometabolic and gastrointestinal set (hypertension, hyperlipidemia, impaired fasting glucose, GERD, diverticular disease/colon polyps). These represent unrelated themes rather than a single clinical phenotype.

phenotypes.label: Type 2 diabetes with complications
phenotypes.description: Type 2 diabetes with metabolic comorbidity and classic complications: poor control, diabetic neuropathy, kidney involvement, and peripheral arterial disease with claudication. Foot and skin infections (onychomycosis, tinea pedis, cellulitis/paronychia) appear alongside hypertension, hyperlipidemia, obesity, and GERD. This pattern skews older and is somewhat more common in males.

phenotypes.label: Neurosurgical postoperative care and complications
phenotypes.description: Cluster of postoperative and postprocedural states centered on intracranial disease, including brain tumors, aneurysms, hydrocephalus, and intracranial hemorrhage. Complications and sequelae such as wound dehiscence, postprocedural infection, persistent postprocedural pain, disorientation, abducens nerve palsy, SIADH, and mononeuropathies suggest recent neurosurgical or neurovascular interventions.

phenotypes.label: Axial spine pain and spondyloarthritis
phenotypes.description: Patients with chronic axial back pain and sacroiliac involvement. Conditions span degenerative spine disease (spondylosis, sciatica) and inflammatory axial spondyloarthritis (ankylosing spondylitis, sacroiliitis), often accompanied by chronic pain syndromes and adjacent joint pain.

phenotypes.label: GI bleeding and iron deficiency
phenotypes.description: Pattern of gastrointestinal blood loss with resulting iron deficiency anemia. Leading conditions include hemorrhoids, diverticulosis, melena, and documented GI hemorrhage, alongside colonic polyps/benign neoplasms, ulcerative colitis, and gastritis or gastric ulcers as bleeding sources. Overall, this reflects recurrent GI bleeding with anemia and bowel inflammation.

phenotypes.label: Migraine and chronic headache disorders
phenotypes.description: Cluster of migraine and chronic headache disorders, including migraine with and without aura, status migrainosus, tension-type and daily headaches. Associated features include neck and myofascial pain, temporomandibular joint disorder, dizziness/vertigo, transient visual loss, and migraine variants (e.g., hemiplegic, menstrual); secondary headache considerations like vertebral artery dissection and concussion also appear. More common in females and skews younger.

phenotypes.label: Dyspnea, chest pain, and palpitations
phenotypes.description: Acute cardiopulmonary symptom cluster with shortness of breath, chest pain, palpitations, cough, and dizziness, often accompanied by tachycardia and ECG abnormalities. Some patients show respiratory failure or bulbar symptoms (dysphagia, diplopia) reflecting neuromuscular involvement.

phenotypes.label: Opioid use, HCV, skin infections
phenotypes.description: Opioid and polysubstance use with frequent overdose/poisoning and substance-induced mental disorders. Complications include chronic hepatitis C and skin and soft tissue infections such as cellulitis, abscesses, and MRSA, with dental abscesses and traumatic wounds also common. More common in males.

phenotypes.label: Prostate disease with urinary symptoms
phenotypes.description: Male urologic disease centered on the prostate, including benign prostatic hyperplasia, prostate cancer with elevated PSA, and erectile dysfunction with bladder outlet obstruction. Urinary symptoms such as nocturia, incontinence, retention, and related genitourinary device complications are prominent. Predominantly affects older men.

phenotypes.label: Parkinsonism with autonomic and cognitive features
phenotypes.description: Movement‐disorder phenotype centered on Parkinson’s disease and essential tremor, with tremor, bradykinesia, dysarthria, dysphagia, and abnormal involuntary movements. Prominent non‑motor features include orthostatic hypotension, constipation, REM sleep behavior disorder, falls, and cognitive impairment or dementia.

phenotypes.label: Plasma cell dyscrasias with neuropathy
phenotypes.description: Monoclonal gammopathy and plasma cell neoplasms (multiple myeloma, Waldenström macroglobulinemia) with peripheral neuropathies and amyloidosis. Associated findings include anemia, hypogammaglobulinemia, bone disease and fractures; related hematologic neoplasms (e.g., MDS/AML in remission) also appear. The pattern skews toward older adults.

phenotypes.label: Chronic kidney disease and ESRD
phenotypes.description: Chronic kidney disease across stages, including end-stage renal disease, with complications such as anemia, hyperkalemia, secondary hyperparathyroidism, mineral–electrolyte disorders, and proteinuria. It also includes hypertensive/diabetic nephropathy, renal transplant status and rejection, and dialysis access complications; within the cohort it is more common in males.

phenotypes.label: Acute abdominal pain and GI symptoms
phenotypes.description: Acute gastrointestinal symptom cluster centered on abdominal pain with nausea/vomiting and diarrhea, often with epigastric or quadrant-specific tenderness. Presentations include biliary disease (cholecystitis), peptic ulcer flares, and inflammatory bowel disease–related complications, frequently accompanied by dehydration and leukocytosis.

phenotypes.label: COPD and tobacco dependence
phenotypes.description: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and emphysema, often with acute exacerbations and lower respiratory infections. Strong linkage to nicotine use, including dependence and remission, with associated dyspnea and reflux symptoms. Mood disorders and chronic pain appear as comorbidities in this group.

phenotypes.label: Prediabetes and cardiometabolic risk
phenotypes.description: Impaired glucose regulation dominated by prediabetes and abnormal blood glucose, with accompanying hypertension, hyperlipidemia, obesity, and vitamin D deficiency. This reflects a cardiometabolic risk profile in adults without established diabetes.

phenotypes.label: Age-related vision and hearing loss
phenotypes.description: Age-linked sensory conditions combining ocular refractive disorders (presbyopia, myopia/astigmatism/hyperopia), early cataract and glaucoma suspicion, with audiovestibular disease (sensorineural hearing loss, tinnitus, benign positional vertigo, Ménière’s disease). This reflects patients with concurrent vision and hearing decline, more common in older adults.

phenotypes.label: Lymphoma with cytopenias
phenotypes.description: This cluster centers on Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphomas (including diffuse large B‑cell, mantle cell, follicular, and marginal zone) with associated cytopenias (neutropenia, pancytopenia, anemia), lymphadenopathy, fever, and fatigue. Common comorbid coding such as hypertension, hyperlipidemia, arrhythmia, and GERD appears, but the defining signal is lymphoma. It skews older and is modestly more common in men.

phenotypes.label: Type 1 diabetes metabolic crisis
phenotypes.description: Acute metabolic decompensation centered on type 1 diabetes, with DKA or severe hyperglycemia/hypoglycemia, electrolyte disturbances (hyponatremia, hypokalemia), dehydration, acidosis, hypotension, and acute kidney injury. It often co-occurs with systemic inflammatory illness (sepsis/SIRS), respiratory failure, and diabetic complications such as gastroparesis, autonomic neuropathy, retinopathy, and albuminuria; this pattern is more common in males.

phenotypes.label: Colorectal cancer postoperative and ostomy complications
phenotypes.description: Pattern centers on colorectal malignancies with consequences of abdominal surgery. Findings include acquired absence of bowel, colostomy/ileostomy presence or malfunction, postoperative pain, and complications such as peritoneal adhesions, intestinal obstruction, hernia, and wound dehiscence. Abdominal pain, constipation, GERD, anemia, and hypokalemia commonly co-occur.

phenotypes.label: Alcohol and polysubstance use with psychosis
phenotypes.description: Alcohol and polysubstance use disorders predominate, including dependence/intoxication and nicotine, cannabis, stimulant, and cocaine use, with alcohol-related complications. Suicidal ideation and self-harm appear alongside psychotic disorders and symptoms (schizophrenia/schizoaffective, delusions, auditory hallucinations). This pattern is more common in males and skews younger.

phenotypes.label: Ischemic heart disease with arrhythmias
phenotypes.description: Coronary atherosclerosis and prior infarction with sequelae, accompanied by heart failure (systolic/diastolic) and cardiomyopathy. Prominent rhythm disorders appear, including atrial fibrillation/flutter, ventricular tachyarrhythmias, and conduction disease, with complications such as embolic stroke and ventricular aneurysm. This pattern skews older and is more common in males.

phenotypes.label: Chronic venous insufficiency and ulcers
phenotypes.description: Chronic lower-extremity venous disease characterized by venous insufficiency and varicose veins with edema, stasis dermatitis, and venous hypertension. Includes postthrombotic syndrome and thrombophlebitis, with complications such as painful leg swelling, cellulitis, and chronic ankle or lower-leg ulcers.

phenotypes.label: Gynecologic cancer with peritoneal spread
phenotypes.description: Coherent cluster of gynecologic and intra‑abdominal malignancies, centered on ovarian and endometrial cancer with peritoneal/retroperitoneal involvement and intra‑abdominal masses. Common accompanying conditions include abdominal pain, constipation, anemia, fatigue, malnutrition, biliary duct dilation, postoperative state, procedure complications (including CLABSI), and urinary infections with dysuria.

phenotypes.label: Venous thromboembolism (DVT/PE)
phenotypes.description: Coherent cluster of venous thromboembolism: deep venous thrombosis with pulmonary embolism and related complications (pulmonary infarction, acute cor pulmonale, respiratory failure). Hypercoagulable states, including hereditary thrombophilia and Factor V Leiden, are prominent contributors. Presentations include limb swelling and pain, chest pain, dyspnea, and abnormal coagulation findings.

phenotypes.label: Bipolar spectrum with insomnia
phenotypes.description: Psychiatric presentation centered on bipolar spectrum disorders across depressive, hypomanic/manic, and remission states, with prominent insomnia. Comorbid mood and anxiety disorders (including OCD, PTSD, and generalized anxiety), borderline personality features, and substance-related presentations (intoxication/withdrawal) are common, with occasional self-injurious behaviors. Nonpsychiatric conditions appear only at low weight.

phenotypes.label: Malignancy with pulmonary nodules
phenotypes.description: Cluster of malignant neoplasms with prominent thoracic imaging abnormalities, notably solitary pulmonary nodules and abnormal lung fields. It includes diverse primary cancers (e.g., stomach, larynx, uterus, testis, bone, soft tissue), calcified lymph nodes, anemia, and postoperative/complication states, reflecting active cancer with associated pulmonary findings.

phenotypes.label: Type 2 diabetes with neuropathy
phenotypes.description: Cluster centered on type 2 diabetes with metabolic comorbidities—hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obesity—and complications such as diabetic neuropathy, hyperglycemia, onychomycosis, and foot pain. Infectious sequelae (urinary tract infection, vaginal candidiasis/bacterial vaginosis, cellulitis) and vascular events (ischemic stroke, malignant hypertension) also appear. This pattern is somewhat more common in men and with advancing age.

phenotypes.label: High-risk pregnancy and obstetric complications
phenotypes.description: Obstetric cluster encompassing confirmed pregnancy with trimester dating, high‑risk and unplanned pregnancy, and maternal–fetal complications. Includes placental disorders (e.g., placenta previa), RhD status, fetal conditions/aneuploidy, and comorbidities in pregnancy such as pre‑existing hypertension, type 2 diabetes, obesity, and anemia. Concentrated in reproductive‑age females and skews younger.

phenotypes.label: Diabetic foot and vascular complications
phenotypes.description: Advanced type 2 diabetes with both microvascular and macrovascular complications. Peripheral arterial disease with claudication, chronic foot ulcers, osteomyelitis, neuropathy/neuropathic arthropathy, diabetic retinopathy (including proliferative disease and macular edema), chronic kidney disease, coronary atherosclerosis, and lower-limb amputations are prominent. The pattern skews male and older.

phenotypes.label: Pituitary adenoma and hormonal disorders
phenotypes.description: Pattern centers on pituitary axis disease: pituitary adenoma and related disorders with hyperprolactinemia, acromegaly/gigantism, hypercortisolism, and hypopituitarism, with secondary adrenal insufficiency and male hypogonadism/testicular hypofunction. Neuroendocrine and other endocrine neoplasms appear alongside systemic findings such as obesity, vitamin D deficiency, malaise, soft‑tissue swelling, and musculoskeletal complaints including tenosynovitis and enthesopathy.

phenotypes.label: Mixed clinical themes
phenotypes.description: This topic blends unrelated themes: chronic PTSD with insomnia and depression; lower‑extremity pain and entrapment syndromes (foot pain, plantar fasciitis/fibromatosis, metatarsalgia, pes planus, trochanteric bursitis, meralgia paresthetica); and extensive dental disease (tartar, caries, gingivitis, cracked teeth). It also includes general comorbidities such as obesity, obstructive sleep apnea, gastroesophageal reflux, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. These conditions do not reflect a single unifying clinical pattern.

phenotypes.label: Knee osteoarthritis and meniscal tears
phenotypes.description: Patients with degenerative knee disease dominated by osteoarthritis, bilateral knee pain and effusions, and meniscal tears. Associated conditions include bursitis, knee instability, soft-tissue injuries, and degenerative changes in other weight-bearing joints, with occasional prosthesis-related complications. More common in older adults.

phenotypes.label: Sleep-disordered breathing and hypersomnia
phenotypes.description: Sleep medicine conditions centered on obstructive and central sleep apnea, snoring, and sleep-related hypoventilation, with daytime hypersomnia and insomnia symptoms. Restless legs and periodic limb movement disorder co-occur, along with narcolepsy/cataplexy and circadian sleep–wake disorders. More common in males and skews older.

phenotypes.label: Fatty liver and biliary disease
phenotypes.description: Hepatobiliary pattern centered on fatty liver (nonalcoholic and alcoholic) with abnormal liver chemistries and hepatomegaly. Co-occurring biliary disease includes cholelithiasis, sludge, cholesterolosis, and common bile duct dilation, alongside chronic hepatitis B and portal-hypertensive features such as esophageal varices and splenomegaly. Pancreatobiliary cysts/masses and benign hepatic lesions (hemangioma) appear with GI comorbidities like gastritis, Helicobacter-associated disease, and GERD.

phenotypes.label: Cataract, glaucoma, and retinal disease
phenotypes.description: Ophthalmic disorders centered on cataract and ocular hypertension/glaucoma with posterior segment disease such as retinal tears/detachment, vitreous degeneration, epiretinal membrane, and retinal vascular occlusions. Uveitis/iritis and ischemic optic neuropathy also appear, with associated visual disturbance and impairment. The pattern skews toward older adults.

phenotypes.label: Lumbar radiculopathy and spinal stenosis
phenotypes.description: Degenerative lumbar spine disease with nerve root involvement. Patients have low back pain, sciatica, and neurogenic claudication associated with disc degeneration, spondylosis/spondylolisthesis, and sacroiliac region disorders.

phenotypes.label: Schizophrenia with metabolic comorbidity
phenotypes.description: Schizophrenia and related psychotic disorders co-occur with prominent cardiometabolic comorbidity—essential hypertension, obesity, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia—with frequent tobacco use. Visits often include chest pain, GERD, cough, dizziness, and headaches, reflecting general medical complaints in this group.

phenotypes.label: Inflammatory skin and adnexal disorders
phenotypes.description: Cluster of inflammatory dermatologic and adnexal conditions, including acne/rosacea, seborrheic and atopic/contact dermatitis, folliculitis and hidradenitis, hyperhidrosis, and hair disorders such as non‑scarring alopecia and hirsutism. This pattern reflects common skin and hair presentations, with prevalence skewing toward younger patients and females.

phenotypes.label: Urticaria–angioedema with asthma and pruritus
phenotypes.description: Recurrent urticaria, pruritic rash, and angioedema predominate, with generalized pruritus and cutaneous eruptions. Concurrent cough, upper respiratory infections, and uncomplicated asthma point to an atopic/allergic diathesis, including chronic or idiopathic urticaria and mast cell–mediated reactions.

phenotypes.label: Pelvic pain and menstrual disorders
phenotypes.description: Gynecologic presentations centered on pelvic pain, dysmenorrhea, irregular or heavy menses, dyspareunia, and vaginitis/cervicitis. Underlying conditions include uterine leiomyomas, ovarian cysts (including corpus luteum cysts), polycystic ovary syndrome, endometriosis, and related causes of abnormal uterine bleeding, with occasional postmenopausal bleeding. Strongly female‑predominant and skewing toward reproductive‑age adults.

phenotypes.label: Urologic hematuria, stones, bladder cancer
phenotypes.description: Urologic conditions centered on hematuria and dysuria, including urinary tract infection, kidney/ureteral stones with hydronephrosis, urinary retention, and abnormal urine findings. The pattern also includes bladder pathology such as mass and carcinoma, alongside bladder stones and diverticula. This reflects patients with urinary symptoms and blood in the urine due to stones, infection, or bladder malignancy.

phenotypes.label: Acute symptom catch-all
phenotypes.description: Nonspecific acute presentations spanning gastrointestinal and cardiopulmonary symptoms with associated distress and anxiety (e.g., nausea, vomiting, chest pain, shortness of breath, wheezing, diarrhea/constipation, syncope). This reflects general complaint visits across the population rather than a single disease phenotype.

phenotypes.label: Cirrhosis with portal hypertension complications
phenotypes.description: Advanced chronic liver disease with decompensation and portal hypertension. Features include cirrhosis (alcoholic, hepatitis C, NASH, autoimmune/PBC), ascites, splenomegaly with thrombocytopenia, esophageal varices, and hepatic failure. Complications include spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, hepatorenal syndrome, portal vein thrombosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, abdominal wall/umbilical/incisional hernias, and liver transplant status or complications.

phenotypes.label: Systemic sclerosis with esophageal and ILD
phenotypes.description: Connective tissue disease centered on systemic sclerosis/CREST with prominent esophageal dysmotility and reflux (dysphagia, achalasia, Barrett’s) alongside interstitial lung disease, hypoxemia, and pulmonary hypertension. Raynaud’s and sclerodactyly reinforce the scleroderma spectrum; advanced respiratory involvement appears with fibrosis, chronic respiratory failure, oxygen dependence, cor pulmonale, and some with transplanted lung present.

phenotypes.label: Depression and anxiety with insomnia
phenotypes.description: Patients carry depressive and anxiety spectrum diagnoses (recurrent major depression, dysthymia, generalized anxiety) with prominent insomnia. Somatic complaints such as limb pain, malaise, and GERD, and tobacco dependence commonly co-occur.

phenotypes.label: Osteoporosis–osteoarthritis with PMR/GCA
phenotypes.description: Cluster of age-related bone and joint conditions: osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, carpal tunnel, and regional joint pain, often with vitamin D deficiency and other bone disorders. It also concentrates polymyalgia rheumatica and giant cell (temporal) arteritis, which co-occur in older adults with proximal girdle pain and stiffness. Overall this reflects an older musculoskeletal–bone health phenotype.

phenotypes.label: IBS with anorectal and colonic disease
phenotypes.description: Cluster of functional and inflammatory gastrointestinal conditions centered on the lower GI tract: irritable bowel syndrome, hemorrhoids (internal/external, bleeding), diverticular disease/diverticulitis, colitis, and benign colonic neoplasms. Presentations include abdominal and left lower quadrant pain, diarrhea/constipation, gas/flatulence, and hematochezia, with some upper GI overlap such as GERD and gastroduodenal inflammation.

phenotypes.label: Chronic rhinosinusitis with asthma
phenotypes.description: ENT-dominant inflammatory airway disease characterized by chronic rhinosinusitis/rhinitis with nasal obstruction and congestion, epistaxis, deviated septum, turbinate hypertrophy, nasal polyps, and reduced or lost sense of smell. It commonly co-occurs with asthma, cough, and bronchitis, with eustachian tube dysfunction and otitis media completing an upper airway cluster.

phenotypes.label: Hashimoto thyroiditis and hypothyroidism
phenotypes.description: Autoimmune thyroid disease with acquired hypothyroidism dominates, including Hashimoto thyroiditis, goiter, thyroid nodules/cysts, and thyroid atrophy. Frequently co-occurs with menopausal and gynecologic diagnoses, vitamin D and B12 deficiency, and bone/cartilage disorders; predominantly affects females.

phenotypes.label: Thoracic imaging abnormalities and lung cancer
phenotypes.description: Cluster of thoracic imaging abnormalities (atelectasis, pleural effusion, pneumothorax) with pulmonary disease and malignancy. Includes solitary pulmonary nodules, enlarged lymph nodes, respiratory tract cancers with metastatic spread (bone, liver) and cancer-related pain, alongside inflammatory and infectious lung conditions (sarcoidosis, coccidioidomycosis) and cancer‑associated thrombosis.

phenotypes.label: Open-angle glaucoma and vision loss
phenotypes.description: Open-angle glaucoma and related ocular hypertension with visual field defects and severe visual impairment, including legal blindness. Cataract and age-related macular degeneration often co-occur, with common cardiometabolic comorbidities (hypertension, hyperlipidemia, type 2 diabetes); the pattern skews older and is somewhat more common in males.

phenotypes.label: Cutaneous lesions and skin cancers
phenotypes.description: Benign and malignant cutaneous lesions dominate: actinic and seborrheic keratoses, melanocytic nevi, pigmentation disorders, hemangiomas, and viral warts, alongside sun-damage findings. Skin cancers across sites are represented (basal cell, squamous cell, and melanoma) with related wound-healing documentation. The pattern skews older.

phenotypes.label: Pediatric ADHD and behavioral disorders
phenotypes.description: Cluster of childhood and adolescent neurodevelopmental and behavioral conditions centered on ADHD with prominent anxiety and depressive disorders. Comorbid features include tics, autism spectrum and developmental delay, conduct/impulse-control disorders, insomnia and bruxism, with some patients exhibiting suicidality, hallucinations, mania, or psychotic disorders. Overall the presentation skews younger compared with other patterns.

phenotypes.label: PTSD with severe depression and panic
phenotypes.description: Trauma- and stressor-related disorders clustered with severe mood and anxiety conditions. Prominent features include posttraumatic stress disorder, recurrent severe major depression (sometimes with psychotic features), panic disorder, generalized anxiety, adjustment disorders, and borderline personality disorder. Occasional somatic symptom presentations and minor intercurrent infections appear, but the core signal is psychiatric morbidity.

phenotypes.label: Type 2 diabetes with complications
phenotypes.description: Type 2 diabetes with poor glycemic control and its complications, including neuropathy, nephropathy with proteinuria, and peripheral circulatory disease. Prominent diabetic foot problems (onychomycosis, ingrown nails, toe pain, ulcers/cellulitis) and hyperosmolar hyperglycemic states appear; this pattern is more common in men and skews older.

phenotypes.label: Morbid obesity with bariatric sequelae
phenotypes.description: Severe/morbid obesity with classic comorbidities, including obstructive sleep apnea, metabolic syndrome, GERD/heartburn, and vitamin deficiencies. It also captures post–bariatric surgery states with malabsorption and related nutritional deficits (e.g., thiamine), obesity hypoventilation with hypercapnic respiratory failure, and excess skin or abdominal wall cellulitis. Gallstone disease appears as an associated complication of obesity or rapid weight change.

phenotypes.label: Systemic lupus with organ involvement
phenotypes.description: Centered on systemic lupus erythematosus with organ involvement—nephritis, pericardial/pleural inflammation, mucosal ulcers—and high autoantibody titers. It includes autoimmune overlap such as antiphospholipid syndrome and Sjögren’s, with comorbid fibromyalgia/chronic pain, chest wall pain (Tietze’s), anemia, and renal disease.

phenotypes.label: EDS diagnosis with multisystem features
phenotypes.description: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome is the central diagnosis here, accompanied by characteristic comorbidities. Findings span musculoskeletal involvement (arthropathy, joint pain, hypermobility, muscle atrophy), functional gastrointestinal disorders, ocular surface and lens disease (tear film insufficiency, cataracts, corneal endothelial dystrophy), and occasional autoimmune overlap such as Sjögren’s.

phenotypes.label: EDS dysautonomia, neuropathy, mast cell
phenotypes.description: EDS patients with prominent dysautonomia (autonomic nervous system disorder, tachycardia, orthostatic hypotension) and peripheral/autonomic neuropathies causing sensory disturbance, foot pain, and balance impairment. Co‑occurring features include systemic mast cell disease with flushing, selective IgG deficiency, syringomyelia, mixed urinary incontinence, and congenital skin anomalies.

phenotypes.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome with hernias
phenotypes.description: Anchors on a documented Ehlers-Danlos syndrome diagnosis with connective‑tissue manifestations such as abdominal wall and umbilical hernias, female stress incontinence, and breast tissue disorders (hypertrophy, fibrocystic change, cysts). Ocular refractive error, osteoporosis, neck pain, edema, mood symptoms, and genetic predisposition are also recorded. Within the EDS subgroup, this pattern is more often noted in older adults.

phenotypes.label: EDS with PCOS and musculoskeletal complications
phenotypes.description: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome with generalized hypermobility and chronic musculoskeletal symptoms, including joint pain, upper‑limb weakness, migraine, and device‑related pain/orthopedic complications, with occasional foot fractures. A concurrent polycystic ovary syndrome pattern is prominent (hirsutism, menstrual irregularity, obesity), with autonomic‑type symptoms such as palpitations and dizziness also reported.

phenotypes.label: EDS hypermobility, injuries, IBS and migraine
phenotypes.description: EDS with generalized joint hypermobility and joint instability, recurrent musculoskeletal injuries (including ribs), and degenerative changes such as osteoarthritis and disc disease. Prominent associated features include irritable bowel syndrome, migraine, a bleeding tendency (qualitative platelet dysfunction with heavy menses), and low bone density/osteoporosis. Within the EDS subgroup this pattern skews older.

phenotypes.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome with cardiac findings
phenotypes.description: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome anchors this cluster, with prominent joint pain/hypermobility and congenital or valvular cardiac findings such as heart murmur, mitral stenosis/regurgitation, and arrhythmia. Additional associated features include thyroid goiter and vitamin deficiencies, with some gynecologic presentations (noninflammatory uterine disorders, postmenopausal bleeding).

phenotypes.label: EDS hypermobility, POTS and GI dysmotility
phenotypes.description: EDS patients with generalized hypermobility show frequent shoulder dislocation and complex regional pain, alongside autonomic dysfunction with syncope and postural tachycardia. Gastrointestinal dysmotility and irritable bowel symptoms are common, with overlapping sicca/Sjögren’s features such as xerostomia, dysphagia, and esophageal dysmotility, plus an atopic allergic tendency.

phenotypes.label: EDS shoulder instability and laxity
phenotypes.description: EDS patients with prominent shoulder involvement marked by joint instability/derangement, ligamentous laxity, and shoulder pain, with related bursal disorders and shoulder osteoarthritis. Some have associated mononeuropathic symptoms and sleep disturbance consistent with a chronic pain burden. Within the EDS subgroup, this pattern is relatively more common in males.

phenotypes.label: EDS pain, dysautonomia, and GI dysmotility
phenotypes.description: Among EDS patients, this pattern reflects hypermobility-associated chronic widespread pain and fatigue with autonomic dysfunction (including POTS-like features) and gastrointestinal dysmotility (gastroparesis, IBS), often with nausea. Pelvic floor dysfunction, dysmenorrhea, and interstitial cystitis indicate a pelvic pain overlap. Within the EDS subgroup it is more common in females.

phenotypes.label: EDS: joint derangement and aortic ectasia
phenotypes.description: Connective-tissue phenotype in EDS with prominent joint derangement and temporomandibular joint disorder, plus joint pain and neuropathic symptoms. Recurrent inguinal hernia and otologic issues (impacted cerumen, bilateral conductive/sensorineural hearing loss) occur alongside cardiovascular findings including thoracic aortic ectasia and nonrheumatic aortic regurgitation, with episodes of bradycardia or tachycardia. Within the EDS cohort this pattern is more common in males.

phenotypes.label: EDS hypermobility, fatigue and neuropathy
phenotypes.description: EDS-specific cluster combining hypermobility-related musculoskeletal injuries (acetabular labral tear, greater trochanteric pain syndrome, hip bursitis, L5–S1 spondylolisthesis) and foot deformities/pressure lesions (tailor’s bunion, callosity). It co-occurs with chronic fatigue and neuropathic features (postviral fatigue syndrome, small fiber neuropathy), sleep disturbance (obstructive sleep apnea, insomnia), and occasional meningeal disorders, reflecting the multisystem symptom burden in EDS.

phenotypes.label: EDS dysautonomia: POTS and syncope
phenotypes.description: Dysautonomia in Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, dominated by postural orthostatic tachycardia, orthostatic hypotension, tachyarrhythmias, palpitations, syncope, and loss of consciousness. Associated features include autonomic dysfunction, migraines and dizziness, gastrointestinal dysmotility (IBS, chronic constipation), systemic mast cell disease, bleeding diathesis (von Willebrand), and occasional brain compression. Within the EDS subgroup this pattern skews younger.

phenotypes.label: Ehlers-Danlos with spinal pain
phenotypes.description: Centered on Ehlers-Danlos syndrome with prominent neck and back pain, cervical/thoracic spine disorders, and chronic pain. Co-occurring features include exercise-induced bronchospasm/asthma, nonulcer dyspepsia, migraine, peripheral nerve disease, and complications of orthopedic implants or fracture nonunion, reflecting connective tissue fragility with multisystem involvement in this group.

phenotypes.label: EDS hypermobility with pain and dysautonomia
phenotypes.description: Hypermobile EDS phenotype characterized by chronic widespread musculoskeletal and myofascial pain with multiple joint involvement, muscle pain/weakness, abnormal posture, ankle instability, and hand/wrist/foot complaints. Prominent orthostatic intolerance with postural dizziness suggests coexisting dysautonomia. Within the EDS subgroup, this pattern is more common in females.

phenotypes.label: EDS hypermobility with hip pain
phenotypes.description: EDS patients with marked generalized joint hypermobility and instability, prominently involving the hips with pain, sprains, enthesopathy, and chronic musculoskeletal pain. Associated features include dizziness/lightheadedness, cervico-occipital neuralgia and headaches, asthenia, and mitral valve prolapse. Within the EDS subgroup this pattern is slightly more common in males.

phenotypes.label: Ehlers-Danlos with skin/vascular fragility
phenotypes.description: Patients coded for Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, with associated features including collapse/syncope, open skin wounds and incisional hernia, and occasional arterial events (carotid dissection, peripheral aneurysm). Asthma and airway complaints are common; metabolic comorbidities (type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia), dysuria, and pain disorders also appear.

phenotypes.label: Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
phenotypes.description: Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (type 3) with marked joint hyperextension, recurrent musculoskeletal pain and instability (patellofemoral, ankle/foot), flat feet, and back/hip pain. Dysautonomia and gastrointestinal complaints are frequent, with chronic fatigue and injury episodes also documented.

phenotypes.label: EDS vascular-valvular disease and GI dysmotility
phenotypes.description: Connective tissue disorder phenotype centered on Ehlers–Danlos with prominent cardiovascular involvement (aortic aneurysm/thoracic aneurysm and mitral/aortic valve disease). Features include easy bruising/ecchymosis, chronic and postoperative pain, and gastrointestinal dysmotility (delayed gastric emptying, GERD), with occasional overlap coded as Marfan syndrome. This captures the vascular and systemic burden characteristic of affected patients.

phenotypes.label: Ehlers-Danlos with migraine and sprains
phenotypes.description: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome with prominent musculoskeletal instability and pain, including upper-extremity disorders, joint pain, and recurrent sprains, alongside sensory symptoms (dysesthesia) and migraine (often with aura). Vascular complications and tricuspid valve disease are also represented, consistent with connective tissue involvement.

phenotypes.label: EDS scoliosis and neuropathic pain
phenotypes.description: Connective tissue disorder pattern centered on Ehlers-Danlos syndrome with spinal deformity (idiopathic and lumbar scoliosis) and widespread chronic pain. Neuropathic features are prominent, including brachial plexus and peripheral nerve disorders, paresthesias, monoparesis, and altered skin sensation; vascular and systemic complaints such as Raynaud’s phenomenon, dizziness, and malaise appear as well. Pelvic and low back pain and occasional gynecologic issues (e.g., polycystic ovary) are noted.
